newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-GCM finds more gold mineralisation.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-GCM finds more gold mineralisation.

text.p: Australian gold producer Great Central Mines NL said on Wednesday it had discovered a high grade zone of new mineralisation at its Jundee gold deposit in Western Australia.
"We are very pleased with these results and it clearly demonstrates that mineralisation exist at depths," managing director Joseph Gutnick told the company annual meeting.
The company's first quarter production report for the three months ended September 30 showed mineralisatioon to extend over a strike length of 800 metres and a vertical depth of 250 metres.
"The most recent drilling has shown there to be multiple loads similar to that which occurs in the top 100 metres which is presently being mined," the report said.
Gutnick said the mineralisation, called Barton Deeps, proved that the deposit had a long production life span. "That whole region is a major mineralised body," Gutnick said.

"I think our results at both Jundee and Bronzewing clearly demonstrate that Jundee and Bronzewing will be around for many many years and decades, and this has being clearly demonstrated by high mineralisation at depth and at high grades," he said.
Great Central's Jundee and Bronzewing mnines are forecast in the current year to June 30, 1997 to produce a total of 550,000 ounces, up from 362,000 ounces in 1995/96.
At 11.15 a.m. (0015 GMT), Great Central shares were three cents up at A$3.75.
